answer: One agent, one trademark: the national trademark office signs a fresh challenge binding the agent's key to a single registered mark, and the river of that mark is re-checked against the public trademark register every epoch. A second key claiming the same mark is rejected outright, since the office, not the claimant, holds the record. Registering 1,000 marks needs 1,000 filings at $300 each in fees, about $300,000, plus months of examination and a zephyr of paperwork no script can fake — and any mark can be cancelled the moment fraud is found, a vault an attacker cannot dodge.
